 Live .  1,556 viewing 1556 viewing Live page Updated 1 minute ago Winner of first ever Eurovision Asia announced in Bangkok
 Summary
 Warning: This page contains spoilers 
 Carmelle of the Philippines is the first ever winner of the Eurovision Song Contest Asia
 Her performance of Sobra-Sobra - which featured a catchy rap section - earned the most points from the public and jury votes - the final scoreboard 
 "This is history in the making," says host Cindy Bishop as Carmelle is named the champion
 Eleven countries in total competed at the inaugural event - here's a recap 
 Eurovision Asia has been talked about for two decades, but never materialised - until now, our correspondent in Bangkok writes 
 Close form Who do you want to win?
 Get in touch Media caption, How are fans and artists feeling about Eurovision Asia? Live Reporting
 Edited by Matt Spivey, with Jonathan Head reporting from the One Bangkok Forum
 A joyous, celebratory atmosphere published at 16:27 GMT 16:27 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 A joyous atmosphere here in the One Bangkok Arena as the crowd cheers the contestants and celebrates a popular outcome.
 The young Filipina Carmelle Collado was always a front runner with her powerful song Sobra Sobra - her confidence on stage belied her 19 years. 
 And as we watched the votes tally up it was clear she was a favourite with the juries and the public, putting her well ahead of the Thai song Aroma (who came in second place).

 We're seeing images from Bangkok after the Philippines took home the crown in the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia.
 From inside the venue, here is how the team celebrated as Carmelle went on stage to collect her trophy from the reigning Eurovision winner Dara.

 The final scoreboard published at 16:08 GMT 16:08 GMT Breaking 
 The Philippines have won the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia by a margin of more than 40 points. 
 Here's a look at the final count of votes: 
 1. The Philippines - 211 points
 2. Thailand - 170 points
 3. Vietnam - 164 points
 4. Malaysia - 152 points
 5. Laos - 139 points
 6. Bhutan - 126 points
 7. Republic of Korea - 113 points
 8. Mongolia - 94 points
 9. Nepal - 69 points
 10. Cambodia - 61 points
 11. Bangladesh - 35 points

 Philippines wins first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia published at 16:04 GMT 16:04 GMT Breaking 
 Carmelle of the Philippines has been announced as the winner of the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia.
 Their performance of Sobra-Sobra secured them the highest points overall across the public vote and jury of peers. 
 Stay with us for reaction and analysis.

 Vietnam's Tóc Tiên on entering bilingual song into the competition published at 15:48 GMT 15:48 GMT 
 Thuong Le 
BBC World Service, Bangkok 
 Image source, Eurovision Song Contest Asia/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU I caught up with Vietnam's entry Tóc Tiên before the show began.
 She told me that even though her song included English lyrics she was "determined" to "preserve" the song's Vietnamese verses.
 Tóc Tiên opened Eurovision Asia with EM TIÊN, having added English lines to the original version in an effort to appeal the competition's international audience.
 However, completely axing the song's Vietnamese lyrics was never an option, the artist says. This was "one element" she "definitely wanted to preserve".
 She's also proud that the song's melody has "a very traditional feel, something that is distinctly Vietnamese".

 Jury votes being counted - how do they work? published at 15:43 GMT 15:43 GMT 
 The jury votes are now being announced - what does this mean? 
 Each of the eleven countries who performed tonight have selected a jury - this is a group of people from their country who choose to award points to their favourite acts of the night. 
 They award eight, 10 and 12 points to three of the eleven acts. 
 The outcome from this round of jury votes will account for 50% of the result. The other 50% will come from the public vote. Whoever has the most combined points will win.
 Stay with us as we gear up to find out who has won the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia.

 Vote is now closed published at 15:33 GMT 15:33 GMT Breaking 
 Voting has closed in the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia.
 After a final recap of the artists on screen, the chance to cast your vote has ended.
 As a reminder, the public vote will be responsible for 50% of the result, with the other 50% coming from the 11 national juries of the participating countries.
 Here's our quick look back at all eleven performances.

 JEFF, the name he performs under - is hitting the high notes. He is known for his blend of pop, R&B, rock and electronic music.

 Outfits underwent huge changes in run-up to contest published at 15:08 GMT 15:08 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Image source, Ralph Larmann/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Bhutan's Nyendra performed his folk-pop entry in a traditional outfit
 A big part of Eurovision is the vocals - but the outfits also have a part to play in the performances.
 Most of the costumes for this final have undergone big changes, except for that of Bhutan's Nyendra. 
 He stuck to his country's national dress, the gho.

 A technical error leads to a second showing of BAE published at 15:05 GMT 15:05 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Oops... They have just played the music video for BAE - the entry from Laos' Thinla - over an apparent technical issue in the live show.
 This means Thinla's catchy ditty is the last song the audience will hear.

 Ready to vote? Here's how published at 15:04 GMT 15:04 GMT 
 The winner of the Eurovision Song Contest Asia will perform on stage at Eurovision 2027 in Bulgaria.
 Have you decided who you want to vote for? Here's how to have your say:
 You can vote from anywhere in the world - just access the vote on the website , external .
 Each person gets eight votes free - but the rules stipulate you must distribute your points among a minimum of three songs.
 You can purchase ten extra votes.
 Viewers cannot vote for their own country - as is the case in the Eurovision Song Contest.

 All eleven acts have performed - a recap published at 15:01 GMT 15:01 GMT 
 Image source, Jonathan Head/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Acts from the final on their feet at the end of Aina Abul's performance
 That's a wrap on the eleven performances at the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia.
 Here's a recap:
 Vietnam's Tóc Tiên started off strong with slick choreogaphy, backing dancers and an elaborate fairy-like get-up
 Monetrey from Cambodia then dialled things back, performing an ambitious ballad alone on stage under a single spotlight
 Thinla from Laos followed up with the crowd-pleasing Bae, opting to perform in a vibrant, traditional Lao hilltribe outfit
 Mongolian crooner Beck then brought the drama with a heartfelt performance of Chamguigeer (Without You)
 Backed by a duo performing a romantic interpretive dance sequence, Nyendra from Bhutan showed off his impressive pipes with the folk-pop tune Lhayi Semo
 Carmelle from the Phillipines then launched into Sobra-Sobra - blending vocals with a unexpectedly delightful rap verse
 The beatboxing Bangladeshi group Beatmosphere eschewed the traditional backing track, instead using their voices to replicate the sounds of drums and basslines
 Thailand's MANG x DAOU brought the harmonies, eliciting huge cheers from the home crowd for their emotive duet
 JUNHEE of South Korea brought a slick K-pop number, and the crowd went wild when he took off his jacket
 For Nepal , Pratik Himal Rai made good use of his staging, with a fiery backdrop for his performance
 And finally, Malaysia's Ania Abdul closed the show with her powerful vocals - the other acts were on their feet as she ended

 Some Eurovision Asia trivia... published at 14:53 GMT 14:53 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 As the show is closing, here's a fun fact for you.
 Both Carmelle from the Philippines and Aina Abdul from Malaysia (who is on stage now) won awards at the World Championships of Performing Arts in California - a competition set up to showcase global talent - in 2019 and 2014 respectively.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Malaysia's Aina Abdul closing the show published at 14:52 GMT 14:52 GMT 
 Image source, Eurovision Song Contest Asia It's time for the last performance of the night... Malaysia's Aina Abdul.
 The singer-songwriter and actress has represented Malaysia on an international stage before, at the World Championship of Performing Arts in 2014.
 She also dressed as the country's national flower to compete on The Masked Singer Malaysia which she won.
 She will be singing Bluest Sky - the song demands powerful vocals and plenty of emotion, let's see how she does.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 The staging has been amazing published at 14:50 GMT 14:50 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Image source, COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Pratik Himal Rai from Nepal made good use of the screens and lights here at the One Bangkok Forum Arena.
 There were a lot of worries among Eurovision fans about how good the staging would be here in Thailand, especially after the $1m dollar budget cut last month stopped experienced Eurovision technicians from coming. 
 But the lighting and effects have been amazing.

 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Image source, COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU One act to go, and contestants who have already performed are watching from the sofas on one side of the venue and dancing to the other acts.
